reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the data-name-1 of GENERATE must name a report group of TYPE DETAIL, optionally qualified (OF/IN) by the report-name whose description holds it; a non-detail report group (page heading, control footing), a subordinate entry, a sum counter, a non-report data item, or a detail qualified by a report that does not hold it is refused, and an unqualified name shared by two reports is a nonunique reference.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel < 2002 picks the cited rule (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1 vs §2023:8.4.2.2.1) in the COBOL1920 ambiguity message; the verdict is the same

reader.edition-search: Read BindGenerate's data-name arm and ReportGroupResolution.Resolve; the only other edition test in BindGenerate (ctx.Edition.DialectLevel < 2002, the §1985:XIII.3.20.3 SR6 detail count) is on the report-name arm, SR2, not this rule. The grammar rules generateStatement / reportGroupReference carry no version predicate (grep of the .g4 files).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the detail-group test, the report-name qualifier and the ambiguity verdict are one path at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise a legal detail GENERATE and the report-group/data-item homonym; not the refusal of a page heading, control footing, subordinate line entry, sum counter or data item, nor a wrong report-name qualifier or a group name shared by two reports.

reader.notes: Conforms. The not-detail and not-a-group diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023:14.9.16.3 SR1 rather than §1985:XIII.4.3.3 SR1 (message text only). A first probe draft without FIRST DETAIL was refused for its page heading (COBOL2199), which is correct at 1985: HEADING and FIRST DETAIL both default to 1, leaving the page heading no lines (§1985:XIII.3.8.4 GR2).
